title: Other boat bands, Bix and Trumbauer in St. Louis, and leaving Marable
summary: How long he stayed with Marable, other boat leaders he worked for, Bix and Trumbauer at the Arcade around 1922, and quitting for California in 1922.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: From about, 1918 afternoon till about around 19. 19, 19, 19, I didn't work with Faith No More on the boat. But I worked on the boat and I went back on the boat with, uh- I worked on the boat with Dewey Jackson. I worked on the boat with Eddie Allen. I worked on the boat with, uh, Charlotte Craig. I worked on the island Queen too, or the Cincinnati. And the captain got all sorted with us. Man, we had the people screaming. And he said, Jesus Christ, you fell in a bunch of sticks. They got us screaming over there. Two boats laying right side, right side, right side, left side. We had a better band on our boat, Faith had it on his boat. Really? Yeah. Did you ever see Bicks in those days? Did he ever come down? See, he was longer longer, Bicks, see, about the 22. Because in 1922, remember when he was running away with my first wife, coming to California, and I went back to St. Louis. Bicks, Trum Boyd, was playing at the arcade. And Pee Wee Russell was playing at the arcade, if Pee Wee ever come here, he'll tell you that. Arcade in St. Louis? In St. Louis. Right on Rock Rock Street. Or Bicks was on the piano. And Bicks lived in Granite City, Illinois, because he used to go to his home. There was a band called the Arcade and Serenaders, right? I don't know what he called his band then. But I know Trum Boyd was playing, he was playing with Paul Whiteman. Sure. Before that, when you- Have you ever seen Trum Boyd? He's dead. Oh yeah? How long? About a year I think. He was no young man either. People you might not remember. But dear That's where Joe knew his band. He had a good band. Yeah. He couldn't mess with them. There's a whole lot of them trumpet players, I'll tell you a whole lot about, I don't say that the list that the guys talk about. I know how much they can read. Because back in them days you had to read in the big bands. You had to read in the big bands. All them bands you had to read. You had to read melodies but like trumpet, clarinets, violets. Your bass and the motion piano players couldn't read so much music. So how long did you stay with Mary?

Well off and on, two years. Off and on. But I worked on a boat more often without fate than I did with fate. See the struggles of people, like when I went, I went back to North, which would go to fate. And I quit fate. I stayed all 1918 till 1920. My dear Ory sent for me. Somebody knocked on the door. Let me see. I quit Faith Band in 22 to go to California.
